name: Guiyang
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Guiyang: data centre and big data partner diligence, data exchange counterparties and bonded zone suppliers.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Guiyang, scoped from Nashville: diligence on data centre operators, cloud and big data partners in Guizhou's digital economy hub, research on counterparties trading through the city's data exchange, and verification of suppliers in the Guiyang bonded zone and development zones.
intro: Guiyang is the capital of Guizhou Province in southwest China, with a population of about 6.6 million in 2024 across six districts, one county-level city and three counties. Its GDP reached 577.74 billion yuan in 2024, up 6 percent. Guizhou was China's first national big data comprehensive pilot zone, and Guiyang with the neighbouring Gui'an New Area has become the centre of that strategy: the digital economy accounted for more than 44 percent of Guiyang's GDP in 2022, the Guiyang Big Data Science and Innovation City counted 1,355 enterprises in 2024, and the city launched China's first big data exchange in 2015. Other industries include automotive manufacturing, modern agriculture and services, organised around several national development zones.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Guiyang mainly because of its role in China's data and computing infrastructure. Companies placing data, workloads or equipment with Guizhou data centres, cloud providers and computing power platforms want to know who owns and controls those operators and how they are connected to state bodies and other businesses. Buyers of data products and algorithms traded through the Guiyang exchange need confidence about counterparties and the provenance of what they buy. Manufacturers, distributors and investors working with companies in the Guiyang bonded zone or development zones seek verification of suppliers and partners. Each of these questions sits within China's strict rules on personal information and data export, which shape what research is possible.

matters.title: Data centre operator diligence
matters.text: Researching the ownership, financing, related parties and regulatory history of data centre, cloud and computing power operators in Guiyang and Gui'an, for companies placing data or equipment with them and for investors and lenders financing the facilities, including links to state-owned groups and local government platforms.

matters.title: Data exchange counterparty research
matters.text: Background research on sellers and intermediaries offering data products, computing power or algorithms through the Guiyang big data exchange, covering registration, shareholders, penalties and disputes, so buyers can judge counterparty reliability and ask the right questions about how datasets were collected and whether they lawfully include personal information.

matters.title: Technology partner and vendor vetting
matters.text: Verifying software, data services and hardware vendors based in Guiyang's big data parks before contracts or licensing deals, including whether they have the capabilities claimed, who ultimately controls them, and whether they or their owners appear in adverse media, litigation or export-control screening results.

matters.title: Bonded zone supplier verification
matters.text: Checking manufacturers, logistics providers and traders operating in the Guiyang comprehensive bonded zone in Baiyun district, through registration data, published judgments and administrative penalties and, where justified, site checks by qualified local professionals, so buyers can assess capacity, ownership and customs-related exposure.

matters.title: Incentive and investment claims
matters.text: Testing statements made by local partners about investment incentives, land, completed projects and government backing in Guiyang's development zones, so investors and joint venture partners understand what has actually been approved and built, and which entities hold the relevant rights and obligations.

local_context.title: National big data pilot zone
local_context.text: Guizhou was designated China's first national big data comprehensive pilot zone, and Guiyang with Gui'an New Area hosts much of its infrastructure: 11 data centres were attracted in 2022 alone, the Gui'an New Area Supercomputing Center offers about 300 petaflops of capacity, and the Big Data Science and Innovation City reported 69 billion yuan of service revenue in 2024. Many operators are closely tied to provincial or municipal bodies, which bears on ownership research.

local_context.title: Guiyang big data exchange
local_context.text: Launched in Guiyang in 2015 as China's first exchange of its kind, the exchange trades data, computing power and algorithms. By August 2024 it reported cumulative transactions above 5.4 billion yuan and more than 1,000 trading entities, and it was targeting annual trading above 10 billion yuan by 2025. Trading data through an exchange does not remove the need to examine the seller and the lawfulness of the underlying data.

local_context.title: Guiyang comprehensive bonded zone
local_context.text: The Guiyang comprehensive bonded zone in Baiyun district was approved by the State Council on 14 September 2013 with a planned area of 10.83 sq km under customs supervision. Its pillar activities are bonded processing, logistics and services, and its listed occupants have included both international and Chinese companies. Entities registered there may operate under particular customs arrangements, which diligence should confirm against their actual activities.

local_context.title: Provincial capital records and courts
local_context.text: As Guizhou's capital, Guiyang is the seat of the provincial government and its departments, and disputes involving Guizhou companies may pass through courts sitting in the city. We have not verified the city's specialised courts or a local arbitration institution for this page, so engagements identify the relevant court records, enforcement lists and administrative penalties with the client's Chinese counsel.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Guiyang, TDSC first defines the commercial question, whether it concerns the controllers of a data centre operator, the reliability of a data seller on the exchange, or a bonded zone supplier's capacity, and then maps the relevant records, including registration data, published judgments and administrative penalties. Research is conducted from Nashville using Chinese-language open sources and commercial databases. Because Guiyang's core business is data, TDSC reviews with the client's Chinese counsel how any personal information or datasets will be handled before work begins, and does not acquire or test data of uncertain provenance. Where site visits are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified local professionals acting lawfully.

faqs.q: How can we check who controls a Guiyang data centre operator?
faqs.a: We trace the operator's registered shareholders and related companies, look for state-owned or local government investment platforms in the chain, and review financing, litigation and penalties of record. The result shows who controls the facility and who may have influence over it, which helps clients assess contractual, continuity and data access risks alongside their technical review.

faqs.q: Is buying data through the Guiyang exchange enough assurance?
faqs.a: Not on its own. The exchange provides a trading framework, but buyers remain responsible for understanding who the seller is and how the data was collected. We research the seller's ownership, history and disputes, and help counsel frame questions about provenance and personal information, which Chinese counsel should review under the Personal Information Protection Law.

faqs.q: Can you verify a supplier in the Guiyang bonded zone?
faqs.a: Yes. We check the company's registration, scope of business, shareholders, related parties, published judgments and administrative penalties, and compare its claims about capacity and customers with public information. Where a site visit is warranted, we coordinate with qualified local professionals and the client's counsel, and we report clearly where records are limited.

faqs.q: Can investigative findings about Guiyang companies be taken out of China?
faqs.a: Research based on public corporate and court records is routinely delivered to clients abroad. Material containing personal information or datasets may be subject to Chinese data export rules, so we agree with the client's Chinese counsel what will be collected, where it will be stored and how it may lawfully be transferred before work starts.

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Guiyang or elsewhere in China. Most of our work is desk-based research. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified local professionals acting lawfully and with the client's Chinese counsel, and we decline requests involving restricted records or covert methods.
